lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says أنا آسف, a woman says أنا آسفة.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the delay.
Sorry for the bother, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian way to answer or check a phone line.

examples.trans: Hello? Jasmine House, how may I help you?
Hello, can you hear me clearly?

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلغ, بيبلغ).

examples.text: في حدا بلغ عن شنتة زرقا؟
examples.trans: Has anyone reported a blue suitcase?
We gave the office the phone number.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتبدل, بيتبدل).

examples.trans: A blue suitcase got swapped at the bus station.
The keys were never mixed up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

ركب.gloss: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly

meanings.en: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركب, بيركب).

examples.trans: We rode the same morning bus!
The new brass thread fitted cleanly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Used in the mild exclamation يا ساتر! ('goodness! / heaven forbid!').

examples.trans: Goodness, I nearly dropped the glass!
Goodness, what heavy rain outside!

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شرايط.

examples.text: ربطت شريطة حمرا على إيد الشنتة.
examples.trans: She tied a red ribbon on the suitcase handle.
I found the ribbon inside the pocket.

meanings.note: Standard everyday 'thank you' across the Arabic-speaking world.

examples.trans: Thank you all very much!
Thank you for your patience, sir.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عناوين.

examples.text: خد رقم النزل وعنواننا لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number and our address, please.
The address is written clearly on the card.

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.
We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أفكار.

examples.trans: I have a great idea for breakfast!
What do you think of this idea?

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لخبطات.

examples.trans: What a strange mix-up with the suitcases!
We sorted out the mix-up calmly and quickly.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Polite way to soften bad news ('unfortunately').

examples.text: للاسف ما في رقم تليفون عالبطاقة.
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number on the tag.
Unfortunately all the rooms are taken tonight.

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: The basic verb for walking, traveling on foot, or things moving forward.

examples.text: الشارع على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The street is five minutes away on foot.
Walking in the morning in Amman is enjoyable.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: معاطف.

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and rest.
Hang the grey coat beside the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine plural noun; مكتب المفقودات means 'lost and found'.

examples.trans: We called the lost-and-found office at the station.
He handed the wallet in to lost property.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناطق.

examples.trans: We rode the same bus to the same district.
This area is famous for its stone houses.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
